findings.finding: The proposed new regression test is underspecified in the mini-plan: it says to assert that the old endpoint is absent and the new endpoint is present. That would pass if the workflow listed open PRs but omitted pagination, filtered on the wrong field, interpolated the SHA incorrectly, or did not feed the resulting numbers into the existing ambiguity guard. It would not fully pin AC2/AC3.
findings.suggestion: Make the structural test assert the meaningful resolver invariants for each `ALL_STAGE2` file: no `commits/.../pulls` endpoint; a `pulls?state=open&per_page=100` request with pagination and slurping; filtering specifically on `.head.sha` against the resolved head SHA; and preservation of the exactly-one-match failure path. This remains consistent with the repository’s structural-test convention while preventing a superficially similar regression.

findings.finding: The head SHA is used in a new `jq` predicate. Even though a normal SHA is constrained, Stage 2 is specifically designed to distrust PR-originated inputs/artifacts, so the implementation must not construct the jq program by shell-interpolating `HEAD_SHA`. Existing checks against raw `${{ github. }}` expressions do not by themselves protect a shell variable populated from an artifact.
findings.suggestion: Pass the value as a jq data argument (for example, `jq --arg sha "$HEAD_SHA" '... select(.head.sha == $sha) ...'`) rather than embedding it in jq source or an unquoted shell command. Add a focused structural assertion for the safe binding form if the existing hardening suite does not already cover artifact-derived shell variables.

findings.finding: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` requires access to pull-request metadata for private repositories. The plan runs the token-permissions test but does not explicitly establish that the Stage-2 workflow has and retains `pull-requests: read`; the former commit-associated-PR endpoint may have had different effective permission behavior.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the workflow’s job/workflow `permissions` explicitly includes `pull-requests: read` and that `test_workflow_token_permissions.py` asserts it for both the repository workflow and shipped template. No broader token grant should be added.

findings.finding: The replacement is necessarily more variable in cost than the single commit lookup: repositories with more than 100 open PRs will make multiple API requests. A transient pagination, rate-limit, or API failure will continue to fail the required context, but may be harder to distinguish operationally from the intentional “zero or multiple matches” fail-closed outcome.
findings.suggestion: Preserve or add clear log/error messages that distinguish an API/listing failure from the ambiguity guard’s zero/multiple-match failure. Validate that the existing shell error handling does not accidentally convert a failed API pipeline into an empty candidate set.  Overall, listing paginated open base-repository PRs and matching `.head.sha` is the correct, simpler resolver strategy for fork heads, and keeping both workflow copies in parity is appropriate. The implementation should tighten the automated semantic assertions and explicitly preserve safe SHA-to-jq binding before merge. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
